notes.togenda: To one person. To a group: Mutagyenda.
notes.hata-kidogo: Na kakye, not even a little.

guidebook.intro: Say no, refuse politely and tell someone not to do something. Runyankore makes verbs negative with ti- at the front.

tips.title: Ti-: not
body: Put **ti-** in front to make a statement negative: **Ninyenda** (I want) → **Tinyenda** (I don’t want); **Nyine** → **Tinyine** (I don’t have); **Hariho** → **Tihariho** (there isn’t).
For “I’m not doing it now” the verb takes **-ri ku-**: **Tindikurya** (I’m not eating), **Tindikugyenda** (I’m not going). For he or she, **ta-**: **Tarikugyenda**.

tips.title: Otagyenda: don’t!
body: To tell one person not to do something, use **ota-** and end in **-a**: **Otagyenda** (don’t go), **Otatiina** (don’t be afraid). To a group: **Mutagyenda**.

culture.title: Saying no gently
body: A flat “no” can sound harsh. People soften it: **Ngaaha, webale** (no, thank you), or **obundi** (maybe), and offer a reason.
